IEE Colloquium on Progress Towards HDTV
abstract: The Independent Television (ITV) Association coordinates many of the activities of the sixteen independent production companies that form the ITV Network. Engineering technical development is an important aspect of these activities, in particular the investigation of new production systems such as HDTV for which an essential requirement must be compatibility with existing 625 line standards. A work programme commenced in 1985 with the acquisition of an HDTV camera and displays to investigate fundamental parameters. Latterly, the ITV Association joined the European Eureka 95 project with the responsibility of providing a complete Studio Reference Chain to the proposed 1250/50 standard.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Progress Towards HDTV
abstract: The MAC signal format in its most basic form will offer improved picture and sound quality compared with existing terrestrial services. The establishment of MAC on the early DBS transmissions will moreover provide the foundation for further developments towards the ultimate goal of HDTV. The first MAC decoders will allow the transmission of wide aspect ratio (16:9) by providing 2 alternative decompression ratios. The next stage will be to increase the bandwidth and adopt a 625 line progressive scan in the display to produce extended definition (EDTV). Finally, the use of HD-MAC will result in high definition (HDTV) transmissions to 1250 line displays. These HD-MAC signals will be compatible with basic MAC reception on non-HDTV receivers, thus allowing the compatible introduction of HDTV.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Signal processing and bandwidth compression techniques
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Progress Towards HDTV
abstract: HDTV pictures are originated, in the Eureka system, using a 1250 line television standard. The bandwidth required by the HDTV source signal, including its colour components, is of the order of 30-40 MHz. Unfortunately the bandwidths of the available distribution media; satellite channels, cable, VCR and videodisc are unlikely to exceed 10-11 MHz. It is clear therefore, that a bandwidth reduction of about a factor of four is required in order to deliver HDTV to the domestic audience. This paper describes the results of research work carried out within the Eureka cooperative project in order to develop a MAC compatible HDTV bandwidth reduction system. The signal produced by this system is termed HDMAC (high definition MAC). Two aspects of this system, digitally assisted television (DATV) and motion compensation, are emphasised in particular. These aspects are instrumental in closing the gap between received picture quality and that available in the television studio, whilst at the same time, allowing a practicable decoder in the domestic receiver.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Progress Towards HDTV
abstract: Previous papers have described the principles of the bandwidth compression techniques that are used by the EUREKA MAC-compatible HDTV transmission system. In this paper, the author briefly mentions some parts of the signal processing needed to recover the HDTV signal which are peculiar to the receiver and then concentrate on the display format and the display devices that will be used for HD-MAC.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
